channel.title: Clinical Research Chaos – open funding calls
channel.description: Open funding calls in clinical research, clinical engineering and rehabilitation, checked on the official text.

item.title: Blueprint MedTech Translator (UG3/UH3 - Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports translational activities and clinical studies to accelerate the development of medical devices for disorders within the missions of participating NIH institutes and centers. Funding covers prototype implementation, non-clinical testing, design verification, and clinical studies. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and foreign organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 28 Jan 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/358823

item.title: Personalised approaches to reduce risks from Adverse Drug Reactions due to administration of multiple medications
item.description: This call supports research to reduce the incidence and severity of Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) resulting from multiple medications. Funded activities include leveraging pharmacogenomics, pharmacokinetics, and biomarkers for patient stratification, alongside integrating health technologies such as artificial intelligence and electronic health records into clinical practice. Proposals should also address clinical utility, guidelines, and regulatory implementation. Interdisciplinary consortia and clinical researchers, with the encouraged participation of SMEs and start-ups, can apply. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-CARE-02

item.title: Portable and versatile Point-of-care diagnostics
item.description: This topic supports the development, optimisation, and clinical validation of portable point-of-care (PoC) medical diagnostic devices adhering to the WHO REASSURED criteria. Proposals should address clear clinical needs, such as resource-limited settings, infectious disease discrimination, or non-communicable emergency care. Funded activities include device optimisation, comparative performance studies against the state of the art, and clinical studies fulfilling EU IVDR or MDR requirements. Applicants designing advanced diagnostic tools may apply. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Stage 1 deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (two-stage call). Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-IND-02-two-stage

item.title: Development of monoclonal antibodies to prevent and treat infections from Filo-, Nairo-, Phenui-, Picorna- and Toga viruses
item.description: This topic supports the development of prophylactic and therapeutic monoclonal antibody candidates targeting specific viruses, including Ebola, Marburg, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever, Rift Valley Fever, Enterovirus D68, or Chikungunya. Funded activities include in-vitro characterisation, in-vivo animal testing, GMP-compliant batch production, and first-in-human clinical safety trials. Proposals should advance existing candidates, with the participation of start-ups, SMEs, and entities from endemic third countries encouraged. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-07

item.title: Integrating climate-related exposures into the human exposome and characterising its changes in response to climate change
item.description: This call supports research strengthening the use of the exposome approach to study global exposures and generate evidence on their health implications, focusing on integrating climate-related factors into exposome research. Funded activities include incorporating multiple climate exposures into exposomics studies, monitoring exposome changes resulting from climate pressures, advanced data analytics, and identifying exposome biomarkers. Collaborative multiscale and multidisciplinary projects involving social sciences and humanities can apply. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-ENVHLTH-02

item.title: Development of predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response by using AI methodologies for chronic non-communicable…
item.description: This call supports collaborative research and innovation projects aiming to develop and clinically validate multimodal predictive biomarkers for chronic non-communicable diseases, excluding cancer. Projects must leverage established artificial intelligence methodologies to integrate clinical data, candidate biomarkers, and real-world data, ensuring trustworthy AI and GDPR compliance. Eligible applicants include multidisciplinary consortia of research organizations, universities, and SMEs, with the goal of advancing personalized medicine and improving healthcare outcomes. Programme: Horizon Europe. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Entities in the EU/EFTA and/or Associated Countries leading prospective clinical studies.. Stage 1 deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (two-stage call). Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-TOOL-01-two-stage

item.title: Development of novel small molecule antiviral therapeutics for pathogens with epidemic potential
item.description: This topic supports the development of novel or existing antiviral candidates targeting specific emerging and re-emerging viruses with epidemic potential, excluding antibodies. Funded activities include candidate discovery, structure-activity relationship optimization, in-vitro and in-vivo characterization, GMP manufacturing, and first-in-human clinical safety studies. Consortia are expected to engage with regulatory bodies, leverage research infrastructures, and encourage the participation of start-ups, SMEs, and entities from endemic third countries. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-05

item.title: Challenge-Driven AI Innovation Booster in Apply AI prioritised sectors
item.description: This funding call aims to drive technological progress and AI adoption in key EU strategic sectors including healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and autonomous driving. Consortia of industrial players and research organizations can apply to organize multi-staged challenge competitions, providing financial support to third-party SMEs and developers creating innovative AI solutions. Projects must start at TRL 2 and reach TRL 5, fostering a strong European AI ecosystem and addressing key goals of the Apply AI Strategy. Programme: Horizon Europe. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 18 Mar 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-CL4-2027-04-DIGITAL-EMERGING-04

item.title: BRAIN Initiative: Brain Behavior Quantification and Synchronization- Next Generation Sensor Technology Development (U01 Clinical Trial…
item.description: This funding opportunity supports the development of next-generation sensor technologies and bioelectronic devices that synchronize with brain recordings to model organismal and human behavior. It aims to foster multidisciplinary collaborations among engineers and behavioral scientists to create reliable, compact, real-time sensing tools. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, governments, and international foreign organizations. Programme: National Institutes of Health (NIH). Projects must advance equipment, scale up to GMP-compliant processes, and perform regulatory work to enable first-in-human clinical studies for repairing complex tissues or vital organs using either in-vitro or in-situ approaches. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON Research and Innovation Actions. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Researchers and multidisciplinary teams including engineers, biomedical scientists, cell biologists, and medical doctors from academia and industry.. Deadline: 16 Sep 2027. Applicants must be US-based established investigators holding a doctoral degree and a named PD/PI role on an active R01 or equivalent NIA grant. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Next deadline: 12 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357000

item.title: Development of Biomarkers or Composite Biomarkers for Neurological and Neuromuscular Disorders (R61/R33 - Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This NIH funding opportunity promotes the discovery and development of candidate biomarkers or composite biomarkers for neurological and neuromuscular disorders. The phased R61/R33 mechanism supports initial proof-of-concept studies and preliminary clinical validation to ensure biomarkers are fit for use in clinical trials or clinical practice. Eligible applicant organizations include domestic U.S. higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit entities, and government bodies. Foreign entities are not eligible to apply. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 22 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356874

item.title: Grants for Early Medical/Surgical Specialists' Transition to Aging Research (GEMSSTAR)
item.description: The GEMSSTAR program aims to support early-career clinician-scientists in medical or surgical specialties to launch research careers focused on aging or geriatrics. It funds transdisciplinary pilot projects and professional development plans within supportive research environments. Only U.S.-based organizations are eligible to apply, as foreign organizations and foreign subawards are strictly excluded from this funding opportunity. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Early-career clinician-scientists trained in medical or surgical specialties.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359940

item.title: NINDS Efficacy and Exploratory Clinical Trials (UG3/UH3 - Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity invites investigator-initiated clinical trials addressing neurological diseases and disorders within the mission of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS). Supported projects include early- and middle-phase exploratory clinical trials as well as later-phase confirmatory Phase 3 or comparative effectiveness trials involving small molecules, biologics, devices, and behavioral or rehabilitation therapies across the lifespan. Various domestic and foreign organizational types are eligible to apply. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Refer to Section III. Eligibility Information in the NOFO for additional information on eligibility.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/360404
